steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Labelling: teachers attach labels to students based on assumptions about ability, behaviour and background. Becker: teachers have an 'ideal pupil' image (middle-class, well-behaved, motivated) and judge students against it. Raynor: teachers labelled students as 'bright' or 'difficult' based on appearance and behaviour, not ability. Labels become self-fulfilling prophecies (Rosenthal & Jacobson: Pygmalion in the Classroom).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Streaming and setting: ability grouping within schools. Streaming: broad ability groups across all subjects. Setting: ability groups within individual subjects. Ball found that working-class and ethnic minority students are over-represented in lower streams. Once placed in a lower stream, it is very difficult to move up - streams become self-perpetuating.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Pupil subcultures: pro-school subculture (accept school values, work hard, aim for qualifications - typically in higher streams) and anti-school subculture (reject school values, disrupt lessons, seek status through deviance - typically in lower streams). Hargreaves: streaming creates anti-school subcultures because lower-stream students suffer a loss of self-esteem and seek status through alternative means.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lacey's concepts: differentiation (teachers label and categorise students as 'bright' or 'thick') and polarisation (students respond by moving towards pro-school or anti-school subcultures). Woods identified more responses: ingratiation (trying to please teachers), ritualism (going through the motions), retreatism (withdrawing), rebellion (active opposition), and colonisation (minimum effort to avoid trouble).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how labelling and streaming can affect students' educational achievement. | Describe how pupil subcultures develop in response to streaming, using Hargreaves' and Lacey's research. | Evaluate whether school processes are more important than external factors in explaining educational inequality.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Labelling -> self-fulfilling prophecy -> streaming -> status frustration -> anti-school subculture -> underachievement. This is the PROCESS of inequality. Pro-school subculture = accept school values (higher streams). Anti-school subculture = reject school values (lower streams). Hargreaves and Lacey. Differentiation (label by ability) + Polarisation (move to extremes) = streaming widens the gap.
